text: Client projects lose days when bug reports arrive mixed with new feature requests. Scope Firewall runs a client project from one team chat on Switch, from the signed contract to the next version.

It starts at kickoff. The Planner turns the client brief into executable rules, asks about what the brief leaves open, and a person signs. Even resetting or signing the contract needs an approval in the room.
Once the contract is signed, the plan shows exactly what the developer still has to build.

Later, the client sends one message with two requests in it: a missing currency, and a PDF export. Reception has no access to the code. It splits the message into two sheets and drafts the questions for the client.
On GO, Reception hands the sheet to two verifiers in two separate rooms. Claude Code verifies, Codex cross-checks blind. Each one runs the signed contract against the live app.
The Planner reads both rooms. They agree: rule F5 fails, so this is our defect, and it is free. A person confirms the severity, and the fix is planned.
The PDF export maps to no rule. It becomes a change request with a quote for the next version, and the signed contract stays frozen.
The client gets one clear update: what is included, what is billed, and what is waiting for their approval.
Delivery goes through staging first. Production needs an explicit approval from the owner, right in the chat.
Bugs stay free, features get quoted, and every release is planned. Scope Firewall, built on Switch.
